# From an ent-Estrane, through a nat-Androstane, to the Total Synthesis of the Marine-Derived Δ8,9-Pregnene (+)-03219A

**Authors:** Zachary A. Shalit; Lucas C. Valdes; Wan Shin Kim; Glenn C. Micalizio

**Affiliations:** Department of Chemistry, Dartmouth College, Hanover, New Hampshire 03755, United States

## Abstract

The total synthesis of (+)-03219A, a rare Δ8,9-pregnene isolated from the marine-derived Streptomyces sp. SCSIO 03219, is described that is based on a series of transformations that enable progression from epichlorohydrin to an ent-estrane, then conversion to a nat-androstane, and finally establishment of the natural product target. Key to the success of these studies was implementation of two rearrangement processes to formally invert the quaternary center at C13 and establish the C10 quaternary center.

## Abstract

Pregnanes have been targets in medicinal chemistry and drug development for decades,1 and there are elegant biomimetic total syntheses of natural products in this class.2 In fact, a large number of medically relevant pregnanes is known, including some of the molecules depicted in Figure 1A [allopregnenalone (recently approved for the treatment of postpartum depression),3a pregnenolone (an anti-inflammatory neurosteroid),3b and hydrocortisone (i.e., cortisol–a target that has substantial history in both chemistry and medicine)].3c–h (+)-03219A (1) is a rare Δ8,9-pregnene isolated from the marine-derived Streptomyces sp. SCSIO 03219 that shares molecular features common to this large steroid subclass4 and possesses the core unsaturated skeleton of zymosterol, an intermediate in cholesterol biosynthesis. Here, we describe the total synthesis of (+)-03219A (1) via a pathway that involves progression from epichlorohydrin to an ent-estrane, then a sequence of rearrangement processes that access a nat-androstane, and finally conversion to the natural product target (Figure 1B). These rearrangements enable formal inversion of the steroidal C13 quaternary center, installation of oxygenation at C17, and realization of the C10 quaternary center.

Our interest in (+)-03219A has sprung from the desire to establish a molecular technology platform of broad utility for the asymmetric de novo synthesis of tetracyclic terpenoids, including steroid-inspired agents. De novo synthesis of steroids, structurally related pharmaceuticals, and natural tetracyclic terpenoids has been an active area of scientific pursuit for well over 60 years.5 While semisynthesis (natural product derivatization) continues to play a significant if not central role in the modern steroid pharmaceutical industry,6,7 interest in realizing efficient, flexible, and wholly synthetic means to such targets has served as continual inspiration for the development of synthetic organic chemistry as a discipline.8 Unfortunately, de novo approaches to the asymmetric construction of functionalized steroidal systems are often unwieldy and limited with respect to molecular flexibility in terms of skeletal substitution and stereochemistry.9,10 Because of the pharmaceutically privileged nature and rich biological profile of molecules in this broad class, we have become interested in establishing fundamentally unique means to achieve their assembly.11,12

Previous studies that played a significant role in sculpting our retrosynthetic strategy toward (+)-03219A (1) are depicted in Figure 2. Metallacycle-mediated annulative coupling between enyne 2 and TMS-propyne 3 provides convenient asymmetric access to the stereodefined hydrindane 4, a molecule that bears the correct absolute stereochemistry at C13 for application to a wide variety of steroidal targets of the natural enantiomeric series. Sequential protodesilylation and matched double-asymmetric Friedel–Crafts cyclization of 4, however, delivers 5, a tetracyclic product with C9,C13 anti-stereochemistry.12b While demethylation of this intermediate and subsequent oxidative rearrangement promoted by the action of PIDA in HFIP delivers a tetracyclic dienone (6) that possesses a C10 quaternary center, the relative stereochemistry of this product is more appropriate for the construction euphanes, limonoids, and retrosteroids rather than marine pregnene 1 and scores of other steroidal targets and unnatural variants that are based on pregnane and androstane skeletons. Furthermore, tetracycle 6 does not possess functionality at C17 to facilitate introduction of the requisite acyl group of (+)-03219A. Unfortunately, attempts to vary the stereochemical course of the Brønsted acid mediated cyclization of 4 have been largely disappointing. As depicted in Figure 2B, the mismatched double asymmetric cyclization of 4 has proven to be wholly unselective with respect to stereochemistry, delivering 7 as a 1:1 mixture of isomers at C9. While recent investigations have led to the discovery that an intramolecular Heck reaction of a related substrate derived from 8 is highly selective for producing the syn-isomer, the product of this reaction similarly lacks C17 substitution to facilitate incorporation of the aforementioned acyl group of (+)-03219A.13

Because of these deficiencies in previously established approaches to the asymmetric assembly of tetracyclic terpenoid motifs through metallacycle-mediated bond-construction and subsequent acid-mediated formation of the steroidal C9–C10 bond, we aimed to establish a new approach to the pregnane skeleton, being inspired by the marine natural product (+)-03219A. Our retrosynthetic strategy is illustrated in Figure 3 and involves five key phases: (i) redox manipulation of androstane 10 and installation of the C17 acyl group, (ii) oxidative rearrangement to establish the C10 quaternary center of 10 from estrane 11, (iii) formal “inversion” of C13 and introduction of a C17 ketone from ent-estrane 12, (iv) alkoxide-directed metallacycle-mediated annulative cross-coupling between 13 and TMS-propyne (3), followed by sequential protodesilylation and matched double asymmetric Friedel–Crafts cyclization, and finally, (v) assembly of enantiodefined enyne 13 from epichlorohydrin and simple organometallic reagents.12b,14

The successful execution of this strategy for the total synthesis of (+)-03219A is illustrated in Figure 4. Alkoxide-directed metallacycle-mediated annulative cross-coupling of 13 with TMS-propyne (3) delivered the expected hydrindane in 65% yield with exquisite control (rr ≥20:1; dr ≥20:1), and subsequent matched double-asymmetric Brønsted acid mediated protodesilylation and intramolecular Friedel–Crafts cyclization delivered the stereodefined tetracycle 12 in 70% yield with outstanding stereoselectivity (ds ≥20:1). To accomplish the required formal inversion of C13,15 ozonolytic cleavage of the tetrasubstituted alkene of 12 delivered the diketone 14 in 61% isolated yield. Dehydration mediated by the action of TsOH in toluene was then followed by intramolecular vinylogous aldol condensation to deliver the tetracycle 11 as a single isomer. Notably, during the course of this sequence, the C13 stereochemistry is established in a stereospecific manner in concert with realization of a C17 ketone.

With the desired stereochemical relationship between C9 and C13 set, a sequence of site-selective hydrogenation of the D-ring enone [RhCl(PPh3), H2], reduction of the C17 ketone, and stereochemical inversion of the resulting secondary alcohol delivered tetracyclic carbinol 15. Demethylation of the C3 methyl ether (DIBALH, PhMe, Δ)16 delivered an intermediate phenol that was converted to the functionalized androstane 10 by the action of PIDA in HFIP.12b Notably, this oxidative rearrangement establishes the C10 quaternary center through a group selective Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement, while also establishing a diene spanning the C and D rings.

Next, attention was directed toward the challenge of selectively functionalizing three of the four alkenes that reside within the tetracyclic skeleton of 10. The challenge of setting the CD-trans ring fusion was addressed by hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation, which was easily accomplished by exposure to Crabtree’s catalyst and H2.17 This stereoselective reduction of the C14–C15 alkene was accompanied by an inconsequential reduction of the C1–C2 alkene to deliver a tetracyclic product bearing a simple A-ring enone. Moving forward, dissolving metal reduction in the presence of t-BuOH resulted in tetracycle 16 that possesses both a trans-fused AB-ring system and a C3 β-hydroxy group. Finally, a relatively straightforward sequence of functional group manipulations comprised of selective silylation of the C3 hydroxy group, oxidation to the C17 ketone, Wittig olefination,18 hydroboration,19 oxidation, and desilylation resulted in the first synthetic sample of the marine pregnene (+)-03219A (1).

Overall, in an attempt to further develop a suite of chemical methods and synthesis strategies of potential value for the de novo construction of tetracyclic terpenoids and synthetic variants of pharmaceutical relevance, efforts focused on the total synthesis of (+)-03219A have resulted in a conceptually unique approach to the asymmetric construction of androstanes and pregnanes. We have shown that metallacycle-mediated annulative cross-coupling and double-asymmetric Friedel–Crafts cyclization sets the stage for a unique progression from an ent-estrane, to a nat-androstane, and finally the targeted marine-derived pregnene (+)-03219A. This success has been made possible through the use of an oxidative dearomatization that is terminated by a group-selective Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement and a unique formal inversion of the steroidal C13 quaternary center by oxidative cleavage/dehydration/vinylogous aldol condensation. We look forward to further exploring the various synthetic transformations highlighted here to achieve asymmetric entries to other classes of tetracyclic terpenoid natural products and related molecules of biomedical relevance.
